assertions.name: derived_W_is_admissible
assertions.source: Both channels' derived weight systems are nonnegative and sum to 1 over the 9 color pairs — the two conditions the Lean class InterNucleonChannelColorTube imposes on any admissible W. So the derived tensor is a genuine instance-candidate, not merely a set of numbers. Would fail if the quantum-dimension mix produced a negative or unnormalised weight.

assertions.name: csb_from_weight_tensor_is_zero
assertions.source: pp and nn both sit in the I=1 triplet and therefore receive identical weights, so the derived weight tensor contributes exactly zero charge-symmetry breaking. Falsifiable consequence: the real ~1% CSB must then come from outside the weight tensor (the corpus names the unwired Coulomb term). Contrast the production sigma/sigma^-1 assignment's ~78%.

description: Bean qou-ml1i: writes out the DERIVED color-tube weight tensor W at q0 (zero free parameters, from PRs #4506 + #4510: isotypic basis T1(x)T1 = A+T1+H, isospin selection I=1 -> T1 / I=0 -> A+H, and the quantum-dimension mix W_A:W_H = [1]_q:[5]_q) and reports the consequences computable without the native trace engine. Checks the derived W is an ADMISSIBLE candidate (nonneg + 9-pair normalisation — the two conditions the Lean class InterNucleonChannelColorTube requires). PREDICTION: pp and nn share weights, so the weight tensor contributes EXACTLY ZERO charge-symmetry breaking — removing the production assignment's ~78% over-break (~78x the ~1% experimental bound) and predicting the real CSB comes from elsewhere (the unwired Coulomb term). NOT TESTED: the deuteron BINDING check needs the per-block Markov trace with the refined generator (pyhecke_native, unavailable in this sandbox); it is left explicitly open with these tensors as its inputs. No target consulted, nothing tuned, nothing wired.
